rationale: Iteration 7 tested base_speed 1.3 with kd 0.40, x = ±0.032 m, kp 3.0 and ki 0.30. Score fell from 372.74 to 269.51. Oval finishes dropped from 19 to 7 of 20, and oval progress fell from 0.997 to 0.920. Progress did rise on the s-bend (0.32 to 0.42) and slalom (0.16 to 0.17), but both still went off track in every run. Steering oscillation on the oval rose to 0.352. The approved feedback set an explicit rule: if oval finishes drop below 15 of 20, or s-bend and slalom progress fall, return base_speed to 1.5 and test kd 0.50 with kp 3.0, ki 0.30 and x = ±0.032 m. Oval finishes fell to 7, which triggers that rule. Slower speed is therefore not the lever to keep. I am reverting base_speed to 1.5 and making one change from the best raced design (iteration 6): kd 0.40 to 0.50. Expected result: oval finishes hold at or above 19 of 20, and oval oscillation may fall because the extra damping works in the direction that raised finishes from 7 to 19 (kd 0.30 to 0.40). The s-bend and slalom remain the main losses. Risk: kd 0.50 may over-damp the tightest bends and lower s-bend and slalom progress. Hypotheses: H1, damping is the productive lever at this spread, so kd 0.50 lifts oval finishes further or holds them. H2, the s-bend and slalom failures come from corner-entry drift, which a further damping step may partly address. Measurements wanted: per-track finish count, progress, oscillation, line-loss timing (bend or straight), max_error location, and oval completion_time.
